definitions.explanation: Describes something grand, impressive in appearance or quality.
Worthy of respect or praise; describes people or their achievements.

examples.japanese: {立派|りっぱ}な{建物|たてもの}ですね。
{彼|かれ}は{立派|りっぱ}な{人|ひと}になりました。
{立派|りっぱ}に{仕事|しごと}をしています。
{息子|むすこ}は{立派|りっぱ}な{医者|いしゃ}になった。
examples.english: My son became a fine doctor.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}から{学|まな}ぶことは{立派|りっぱ}なことです。
examples.english: Learning from failure is an admirable thing.

examples.japanese: {立派|りっぱ}な{庭園|ていえん}がある。
{立派|りっぱ}な{家|いえ}に{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: They live in a magnificent house.

examples.japanese: {立派|りっぱ}な{大人|おとな}になってね。
{立派|りっぱ}な{業績|ぎょうせき}を{残|のこ}した。
{立派|りっぱ}な{態度|たいど}で{対応|たいおう}した。
examples.english: They responded with a respectable attitude.

examples.japanese: {立派|りっぱ}なお{寺|てら}を{見|み}に{行|い}きました。
examples.english: I went to see a magnificent temple.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{立派|りっぱ}なビルが{建|た}ちました。
examples.english: A splendid building was built in front of the station.

notes:
{立派|りっぱ} is a na-adjective describing something worthy of respect or admiration.

FORMS:
- {立派|りっぱ}な + noun: a fine/splendid ~
- {立派|りっぱ}に + verb: admirably, splendidly
- {立派|りっぱ}だ/です: is splendid

TWO MAIN USES:
1. Physical impressiveness: {立派|りっぱ}な{建物|たてもの} (magnificent building), {立派|りっぱ}な{庭|にわ} (splendid garden)
2. Moral/character praise: {立派|りっぱ}な{人|ひと} (respectable person), {立派|りっぱ}な{態度|たいど} (admirable attitude)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {立派|りっぱ}に{育|そだ}つ: to grow up well
- {立派|りっぱ}な{大人|おとな}になる: to become a fine adult
- {立派|りっぱ}に{成功|せいこう}する: to succeed admirably

Often used when praising someone's growth or encouraging children about their future.
